answer.rationale: Rollback_release is explicitly disallowed by the compliance constraint, so the 90-min p99 climb on the write path cannot be addressed by reverting the 2-hour-old security-patched release. Add_capacity would be slow to provision (the retail-peak headroom story in memory_b3 was about planned ahead-of-time provisioning, not rapid on-the-fly response). Regional_failover during settlement peak with heavy writes risks customer write loss — the constraint we must avoid — and the March incident was latency-driven, not write-path saturation. Enable_circuit_breaker would start shedding writes at the exact moment settlement traffic is at its daily peak, threatening customer writes. Memory_b5 (day 55) already validated the pattern for this situation: when write-path latency degrades under load, routing report/dashboard read traffic to read replicas removes the extra read pressure from the primary, letting the primary commit transactional writes faster. In memory_b5, transactional write latency recovered the same day with no write loss — precisely the outcome needed now. Because this is the only direction that both (a) relieves pressure on the write path without dropping writes, (b) leaves the mandatory security patch in place, and (c) is fast to enact at the routing layer, it is the one intervention I can spend right now. I will verify memory_b5 before committing to confirm the prior recovery was full and durable, and will scope the intervention to read/report traffic only, monitoring p99 write latency for the first 15 minutes before widening the route split.
